promoteRoleFindings renames .part to the final name only on exit 0, so a role unit that died leaves only a .part and the oracle's predicate (which reads the final name) re-runs it. Live run showed final names only for the roles that exited 0.

Ran it: a single unmetered runner printed 'spend is not metered: the runner declares no spend_key ... run_max_budget_usd is inert' once at run start; a map {implement:claude, default:opencode} named the seven unmetered kinds. Not printed for --dry-run.
Ran it: with $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-impl.ndjson.part holding a valid JSON object the hook exits 0 — the hook reads the .part, since it runs inside the child before the driver's rename.
Ran it: tp run --status --compact kept stop_reason, units_done, wall_clock_seconds, spend_usd and the caps object, and dropped last_unit (the only per-unit row and the only log path).

Ran all three: --resolved reported all seven with source; --extract hoisted the five numerics and runner into .tp/config.json; --project reported run_max_units as a deviation when the task override differed. notify_cmd is documented as absent by construction from --extract/--project because §7 reads it from .tp/local.json only.
TestRunDriver_EmptyNextUnitsStopsWithNoUnits passes; the loop returns on the first empty array rather than re-polling.

Ran it: runner.cmd=/nonexistent/harness stopped the run with driver-error and exit 4, with the unit's run-state row left at null exit_code (not charged an attempt). TestRunDriver_ARunDirectoryItCannotWriteIsADriverError covers the second cause.
Ran it: run_max_unit_retries=1 produced exactly two attempts (seq 1 and 2, attempt 1 and 2) for the same failing unit before unit-failure.
Ran it: with a run in flight (sleep 3s children), tp set t1 estimate_minutes=6 succeeded while a second tp run exited 4 with 'another tp run holds .tp/locks/run-spec.lock'.

No memory layer exists: no embeddings/vector store anywhere in internal/. The only cross-unit continuity is the single last_failure object; tp resume is the handoff. Ran tp resume --json on /tmp/tp-a7/p3 after a failed run and read the whole state back from disk.

Fresh-per-unit is the driver's shape (driver.go spawnAll) and a failed verification reaches the next unit: ran a run with TP_FAKE_RUNNER_EXITS=3,3, then tp resume and tp next --brief both surfaced the same last_failure record with exit_code 3.

No completion-string match anywhere in the driver; the exit condition is the oracle's phase==release. Observed live: a converging fixture stopped only when BuildNextUnits/phase said so, and stop_reason came from stopreason.go's closed vocabulary, never from child prose.

Only StopConverged is reached by agreement; the three caps are backstops. Ran cap-units, cap-wall-clock and cap-budget arms in the engine suite plus a live unit-failure run — no cap recorded a round or marked a phase converged.

Ran all four user-only ops under TP_UNATTENDED=1 live: each exit 2 with an escalate hint. hooks/pre-tool-use-write-deny.sh denies the fence and hooks/hooks.json declares timeout 10 on every hook. §5.1/§6.2/§6.4 all present.

Live: a runner writing to stdout/stderr had both redirected into .tp/runs/<id>/1-implement-t1.jsonl and nothing reached the driver's own output; cmd.Stdin=nil closes stdin; run_max_unit_budget_usd bounds spend per unit via the claude template's flag.

Live run recorded three audit-role children with overlapping spawned_at timestamps (21.516196/21.516249/21.516413) while the audit-record child spawned only after all three exited. Only the two role kinds are Concurrent().
Runner.Cmd is the executable and the only required field. Live: a runner object {cmd:/tmp/tp-a7/talker.sh} spawned that binary; an object without cmd is a RunnerShapeError (exit 2).

All five placeholders are defined and resolved by ExpandArgs; an unknown braced placeholder is a usage error naming runner.args[N]. Live: args ['{unit_kind}','{unit_id}','{log_path}','0'] expanded to implement/t1/<abs log>/0 in the recorded child argv.

Ran it: runner.env {TP_UNATTENDED:0, TP_RUN_ID:HACKED, MY_EXTRA:yes} produced a child seeing TP_UNATTENDED=1, TP_RUN_ID=<real ULID>, MY_EXTRA=yes. env merges over the parent and the driver's own vars win.

Live: seam runner declares spend_key total_cost_usd; TP_FAKE_RUNNER_SPEND=0.42 gave two rows spend 0.42 and totals.spend_usd 0.84. A runner declaring none reported 'spend is not metered' once at run start and spend null.
implement -> taskIsDone(TaskFile, ID); Concurrency() returns alone. Live: two implement units ran in separate iterations, never overlapping.
review-role -> roleFindingsParse($TP_ROUND_DIR/role-<id>.ndjson), parallel with siblings. Live run left role-<id>.ndjson files in .tp/rounds/spec/audit-r1 after the driver's rename from .part.
review-record -> merged.ndjson AND the review round file for TP_ROUND both exist; Alone. Both halves are plain existence checks (fileExists), so the predicate is decidable with no baseline.

review-resolve -> allRowsDisposed(merged.ndjson): every row carries the `resolved` object; Alone. Confirmed the disposition key is the same one tp review/audit --resolve writes (observed in a live --resolve run).
decompose -> taskFileHasTasks: at least one task; Alone. The init shell holds zero tasks, so an import that wrote nothing is not a completed decompose.
audit-role shares the role predicate and the sibling-roles concurrency. Live run spawned spec-coverage, security and maintainability-conventions together and each wrote its own file.
audit-record -> merged.ndjson AND the audit round file for TP_ROUND; Alone. Live run scheduled it alone after all three role children exited.

audit-fix -> rowIsDisposed(merged.ndjson, role:item_id); Alone. Ran tp audit --resolve res.ndjson spec-coverage:i1 wontfix with no code change and the row gained `resolved`, which is the whole predicate.
StopConverged is produced only by the oracle reporting phase release (driver.go RunDriver). TestRunDriver_StopsConvergedWhenTheOracleReportsRelease passes.
cap-units compares against totals.Units, which counts attempts. Verified live: a unit retried once produced totals.units 2 and --status units_done 2 for one distinct unit.
cap-wall-clock compares elapsed seconds against run_max_wall_clock_seconds (TestRunDriver_CapWallClockStopsTheRun, passing).
cap-budget accrues from metered rows only and is inert at 0 (TestCapStop_BudgetAccruesFromTheMeteredRows, TestRunDriver_UnmeteredRunnerReportsNullAndLeavesCapBudgetInert, both passing).
Ran it: TP_FAKE_RUNNER_ESCALATE=1 produced stop_reason escalation on the first attempt, no retry, and the record at .tp/runs/<id>/1-escalation.json left in place.
Ran it: a unit that never wrote its durable write was attempted twice (run_max_unit_retries=1) and then stopped the run with unit-failure; the run state showed seq 1 and 2 for the same (kind,id).
no-units is produced when next_units is [] on a non-releasable cycle. Confirmed against tp's own repo, where a spec-stale escalate blocker yields next_units [] in the audit phase.
SIGINT/SIGTERM set interrupted; TestRunDriver_SignalStopsTheRunWithInterrupted and TestRunDriver_SignalDuringAnAttemptSpendsNoRetry both pass in ./internal/engine.
Ran it: runner.cmd=/nonexistent/harness gave exit 4, stop_reason driver-error, and the unit's run-state row kept exit_code/duration/spend null rather than being charged an attempt.
Ran it: TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp done t1 "reason" --skip-gate "why" -> exit 2, error names it a user-approved decision, hint 'tp escalate --decision skip-gate'. Without the variable the same call proceeds.

Ran it against a resolved 5: review_max_rounds=8 and audit_max_rounds=8 each exit 2 naming the resolved value and the matching escalate decision; =5 is accepted; the project layer is refused identically.
Ran it: TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp import file --force -> exit 2, 'tp import --force is a user-approved decision and is refused under TP_UNATTENDED', hint naming --decision import-force.
Ran it: run_max_units=200 above a resolved 7 exits 2; run_max_budget_usd=0 while 5 resolves exits 2 (0 means disabled for the budget fields); equal or lower values exit 0.

hooks.json registers SessionStart with matcher '*'. The script preflights tp's presence and its version against .claude-plugin/plugin.json's, failing with the brew/go install lines, then prints tp resume --compact as the only payload.
hooks.json matcher is 'Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit'. TestPreToolUseHookDeniesTheFencedPaths, ...AllowsOrdinaryWrites and ...DoesNotFireForShellWrites all pass, covering the four fenced classes.
Ran the hook's whole decision table by hand: no file exit 2, valid 0, malformed 2, blank-only 0, trailing garbage 2, escalation present 0, non-role kind 0, stop_hook_active true 0, no TP_ROUND_DIR 2.
Ran it: default 100 (tp config --resolved source 'default'); 1 and 10000 accepted, 0 and 10001 both rejected with 'must be between 1 and 10000'.
Ran it: default 28800; 60 and 604800 accepted, 59 and 604801 rejected with the documented range message.
Ran it: default 0; 0 and 10000 accepted, 10001 rejected. 0 leaves cap-budget inert (engine/driver.go capStop).
Ran it: default 0; 0 and 1000 accepted, 1001 rejected. BuiltinRunner appends --max-budget-usd only when the value is > 0, so 0 omits the flag pair rather than passing a literal 0.
Ran it: default 1; 0 and 5 accepted, 6 rejected. A live run with retries=1 attempted the failing unit exactly twice.

Ran it: tp config --resolved reports runner default 'claude' (source default); a task-file workflow runner:'opencode' resolves with source 'override'; ResolveRunner accepts a name, a cmd-bearing object, or a per-kind map.
Ran it: notify_cmd is unset by default and read only from .tp/local.json's top-level key (source 'local'); a notify_cmd inside a task file's workflow block is ignored, exactly as §7 states.

wrapArityErrors walks the whole command tree after cobra's built-ins are registered. Ran it: tp show/close/reopen and cobra's own `tp completion bash extra` all exit 2, and tp show's hint names the missing argument from its Use line.

Ran it: --resolve and --resolve-all write the same `resolved` object as their review counterparts with the same three dispositions and --force; the selector accepts a 0-based index and a role:item_id key. A no-code-change disposition satisfies rowIsDisposed.

Ran it with 60 changed files: file_summary reported total_files 50, total_changed 60 and truncated true, the notice named both numbers, and --quiet left the two payload fields intact. truncated is derived from the counts, not from which resolution path ran.

Every kind's brief_command matches §3.3.1 verbatim, including the record kinds' guarded merge step. Succeeded() is exit 0 AND the durable write; both single-sided cases were observed as failed attempts in a live run.
Caps are evaluated between iterations; no kill call exists in the driver. SIGINT/SIGTERM set interrupted, in-flight children finish, and runIteration withholds a retry once signalled.

Ran it and read the recorded environments: TP_RUN_ID a ULID, TP_RUN_DIR absolute, TP_ROUND_DIR from phase+round, TP_FILE resolved, plus TP_UNIT_ID/KIND/SEQ/PHASE. Round vars absent outside a round phase; driverEnv applied after the runner.env merge.

README carries tp run in the command index, a paragraph on the loop and the runner configuration (built-in claude/opencode templates and a runner object), the TP_UNATTENDED restrictions with tp escalate, and the plugin's installation and hook behaviour. SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md carry every field name; CLAUDE.md's reset-native section is rewritten around tp run with subagent-per-unit as the interactive fallback.

Ran it: an unexecutable runner.cmd stopped the run with driver-error and exit 4; record() skips FinishUnit for such an attempt so the row keeps its nulls and no unit is charged. An unwritable run directory takes the same path.

Ran a live cycle: the loop read the cycle state, took next_units, spawned the three role kinds together and every other kind alone, re-read the state from disk between iterations, and checked caps. Crash resumption is covered by TestRunDriver_CrashedDriverResumesAtTheSameUnit.

Ran it: a valid record stopped the run with escalation on an exit-0 harness, was not counted as a failed attempt and left no last_failure. Validate() is strict about every documented field, and TestRunDriver_InvalidEscalationRecordIsAnOrdinaryAttempt / _ExitTwoWithNoRecordIsAnOrdinaryAttempt both pass.

Ran git check-ignore in a fresh tp init project: all four artifact classes are ignored. The shipped .tp/.gitignore carries local.json, locks/, run-*.json, runs/, rounds/, last_failure-*.json — the four new entries beside the two that existed.

The hook reads the minimum out of plugin.json, compares it against tp --version with a numeric dotted comparison, and fails with the brew/go install lines when tp is absent or older; otherwise it prints tp resume --compact. Registered for matcher '*'. All five session-start tests pass.

Ran the full decision table by hand: fires only on *-role, applies the parse predicate to the unit's .part, checks the escalation record, blocks with neither, allows with either, never fires for a non-role kind, and stands down on stop_hook_active.
All three hooks.json entries and both role-agent hook declarations carry timeout: 10. TestEveryShippedHookDeclaresTheBound, _TerminatesOnAdverseInput and _FailsClosedInsideTheBound all pass.

hooks.json registers it for Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit only, so shell writes (and tp's own) are outside the matcher. The four fenced classes are covered by TestPreToolUseHookDeniesTheFencedPaths, which passes alongside the allow and escaped-argument cases.

Ran both arms: gate failure with TP_UNIT_KIND set wrote last_failure with the gate's own output as summary; the identical call without the variable wrote nothing and left the shipped command unchanged.

Ran it: a non-zero exit wrote .tp/last_failure-spec.json with the six documented fields and a tp-authored summary naming the command and log rather than copying prose; tp resume and tp brief both surfaced it; ClearLastFailure matches on (kind,id).

Ran it: location_clusters carried {location, roles, severities, count} for the location two roles reported and omitted the single-role one; merged_count, the clean flag and the --status --check exit code were unchanged.

MechanizePhaseQualifier is appended by next_action's mechanize branch only, and the identical sentence appears exactly twice in skills/tp/SKILL.md (the mechanize-candidate rule and Workflow D step 3), verified by exact substring count.

Ran both merges: inputs [{path,parsed,skipped}] per file; an input with content lines and none parsed exits 1 with the re-emit hint; zero-byte and blank-only inputs exit 0; blank lines are neither parsed nor skipped so they never trigger the condition.

Ran tp resume --json: next_units carries {kind,id,brief_command} with round alongside, next_action.payload.unit renders next_units[0], and soloIfNotConcurrent guarantees a non-concurrent kind is never returned beside another unit.

Ran it on two different stop reasons: fired both times, exec'd without a shell (strings.Fields), carried TP_STOP_REASON and TP_RUN_ID always and TP_ESCALATION_PATH only on the escalation, and its own exit 7 was reported without changing stop_reason.

agents/ declares tp-implementer, tp-reviewer and tp-auditor; the two role agents register the write allowlist hook and the implementer deliberately does not. Probed the allowlist live: only the role's own .part and its escalation record are permitted, everything else denied. agentByKind appends --agent per kind and none for the rest.

Ran `claude plugin validate .`: Validation passed. plugin.json sits beside marketplace.json and declares identity and version 0.35.0; skills/tp, hooks/ and agents/ are at the same root and no binary is shipped.

The record unit is emitted only when the panel is non-empty, every role in it satisfies the predicate, and the round file is absent; an empty or unresolvable panel returns none, keeping its emptiness a no-units stop. Observed live: a collected audit round produced exactly one audit-record unit for round 1.

Ran it: 1 + run_max_unit_retries attempts, each with a fresh seq and log path; clearUnitArtifacts deletes a role unit's findings file and any stale .part immediately before each spawn, so a leftover cannot satisfy the retry's predicate.

Ran it: under TP_ROUND_DIR both tp review and tp audit emit $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-<role>.ndjson.part per role, in output_path and in the prompt text; without it the emitted name is unchanged. The record brief merges role-*.ndjson and writes merged.ndjson only when absent.

roundBasedUnits omits every role whose file satisfies the predicate and keeps a malformed one pending; after a round is recorded, dispositionUnit returns one audit-fix at a time or one review-resolve while any finding lacks a disposition.
Ran it: --compact kept stop_reason and the cap totals and dropped last_unit, which is the only per-unit row and the only log path in the payload.
Ran it: --dry-run printed the units the driver would execute next, exited 0, spawned nothing (no invocation records) and wrote no run state; TestRunDryRun_TakesNoRunLock pins the lock half.

Ran it: converged exits 0 and every other stop_reason exits 4 (observed for unit-failure, escalation and driver-error); a usage error before the loop starts exits 2 (a bad runner shape or template name).
Ran it: the lock is .tp/locks/run-<base>.lock, held for the whole run; a second tp run exited 4 with a hint naming the cycle, and a child's own tp set write succeeded at the same moment.

Ran it: .tp/run-<base>.json carries run_id, started_at, phase, stop_reason, totals and one row per attempt, written through writeFileAtomic (temp+rename). A row is appended with nulls before the spawn and updated after; totals restart at zero on a new run.

Ran it: --status printed phase, units_done, spend against each cap, the last unit's exit code and log path, stop_reason and run_state; all three run_state arms observed plus the new unprobeable-lock arm. Exit 0 when it can report, 3 when no run state exists, and it takes no lock.

Ran it: TP_RUNNER_SEAM short-circuits ResolveUnitRunner before the field is resolved at all, its args are the four positional placeholders and its spend_key is total_cost_usd. The fake runner recorded argv, environment, spawned_at and exited_at for every invocation.

ResolveRunner tells the three shapes apart by JSON: a string is a template name, an object with cmd is a runner, any other object is a per-kind map validated whole. A map without default and a runner object without cmd are both RunnerShapeError (exit 2 with the three-shape hint).

Ran it: spend read from the final log line under the declared key (0.42 per row, 0.84 accrued); a runner with no spend_key reported null and the 'not metered' notice once at run start; a per-kind map named its unmetered kinds.

The claude argv is -p {prompt} --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode auto, with --max-budget-usd appended only when run_max_unit_budget_usd > 0; opencode is ['run','{prompt}']. ResolveUnitRunner is pure and runs in prepare() before any spawn, so an unresolved placeholder is raised first.

stopPrecedence is the spec's sentence in order, with converged leading; highestPrecedence takes every satisfied condition rather than testing in call order. The converged-outranks-a-cap and converged-outranks-an-escalation tests both pass.

Nine values as a named type; RunRecorder.Stop refuses anything outside the vocabulary. Observed converged-adjacent, unit-failure, escalation, no-units and driver-error live; the three caps are covered by their own passing tests. No stop path records a round.

Ran it: the record at $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json carried all seven documented fields, the command exited 2, a sixth decision value was a usage error, two seqs wrote separate files, and outside a run it is exit 2.

Ran every arm: the four ops exit 2 under the variable and 0 without it; an equal or lower cap is accepted; a budget field set to 0 while a non-zero value resolves is refused; runner and notify_cmd are refused at every layer with their own message; activation is any present non-empty value other than 0.

Eight kinds in table order with their predicates and concurrency; each predicate reads named artifacts with no baseline; the role predicate skips blank and whitespace-only lines. Verified by running the twin implementation in the Stop hook across the same inputs.

Ran it: a template omitting {log_path} had both streams redirected to $TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl (verified by reading the file's contents); one using the placeholder owns the file. cmd.Stdin=nil closes stdin for every child.

Ran it: all seven fields resolve with their documented defaults; every numeric field accepted both endpoints and rejected one step outside each; notify_cmd resolved from .tp/local.json's top-level key only. --resolved, --extract and validate --project each covered them.
